$comment: Machine-readable delivery status for every requirement ID in
docs/functional-requirements.md, in spec order. Read by tools/fleet to decide
what to queue next. It is a work list, not a source of truth: docs/spec.md and
the README are, and where this file disagrees with one, this file is wrong.
A bare "partial" is rejected: the remaining line is the only part a later pass
cannot work out by reading the repo.
One line per ID, and every ID is always present, so landing a requirement is a
single-line edit rather than an insert - two branches changing different IDs do

ACME-002.remaining: Renewal is decided but cannot be persisted. acme.EnsureValid correctly reports when a certificate is due (two-thirds of lifetime) and issues a replacement, and status warns inside 14 days of expiry, but a renewed certificate has nowhere to go: keystore.Writer.Store refuses to overwrite a key that already has content by design, the same invariant that keeps SECRET_KEY/INTERNAL_TOKEN/the SSH host key from silently rotating (spec.md 'Identity'). Renewal therefore returns a valid certificate to its caller while the bundle keeps the old one, and the next call renews again. Closing this needs a write path for renewal-eligible key material that does not loosen the no-overwrite guarantee for keys that must never rotate, which is an open decision. This is not what makes re-running up unsafe: UP-003 is closed by reading the persisted certificate through EnsureValid, which needs no write at all.

UP-003.remaining: configureTLS still re-issues a fresh certificate from a new ACME account on every up, risking Let's Encrypt's duplicate-certificate rate limit on repeated re-runs. The read side to fix it exists (the certificate init persists via INIT-003, and the renewal-aware acme.EnsureValid from ACME-002), but there is no write side: keystore.Writer.Store refuses to overwrite existing key material by design, the same invariant that keeps SECRET_KEY/INTERNAL_TOKEN/the SSH host key from silently rotating, so a renewed certificate has nowhere to be persisted back to. Needs an architecture decision (Evan's call) on how a renewal-eligible key gets a distinct update path without loosening that guarantee for keys that must never rotate silently. See docs/tech-spec.md 'Known gap' under Deployment.
